title: Budget forecast exports and alert heuristics
body:
PURPOSE
Quick working notes and wireframe writeup for budget forecast exports + alert heuristics. This doc captures product decisions, proposed UI components, export CSV shape, alerting behavior, and outstanding grooming items. Intended for design, infra, and eng squads working on the billing console sprint (sprint 42).

BACKGROUND
- Customers ask for two gaps: (1) more actionable CSV exports that include forecasted spend and allocation rollups, (2) smarter alerting to reduce noise while preserving SLA for cost events.
- Existing export is a simple per-invoice dump. We need forecast-aware exports and an alerts system that understands allocation hierarchies (projects, teams, cost-centers).

PROBLEM STATEMENT
- Export consumers (finance, FP&A) currently do manual joins to add forecast or commit data. This leads to errors and prevents chargebacks automation.
- Alerting today is token-count or raw-cost threshold only, leading to many false positives from ephemeral usage spikes.

GOALS
- Provide an export that includes: historical usage, model-level burn, remaining budget, 30/60/90-day forecast columns, and allocation attribution.
- Expose a UI for configuring alert heuristics: adaptive thresholds, lookback windows, cool-downs, and scope (project/team/global).
- Keep initial rollout self-serve for Hosted customers; Dedicated/Private customers get same UX but with additional export retention controls.

USER STORIES (PRIORITIZED)
1) As an FP&A analyst, I want a CSV export that includes forecast columns so I can reconcile monthly invoices with projected spend.
2) As an eng manager, I want alerts only when spend is sustainably trending above expected (not on day-one spikes).
3) As a billing admin, I want to export allocation hierarchies joined to spend so I can push chargebacks into our accounting system.

WIREFRAME NOTES (sketch-level)
- Screen: Budgets > Budget Detail > Exports & Alerts tab (new)
  - Top row: quick stats (budget limit, burn-to-date, forecast-30d, forecast-90d, remaining). Small sparklines for last 14 days.
  - Export block (left): presets dropdown (Monthly reconciliation, Chargeback CSV, Forecast snapshot), custom CSV builder (drag fields or checkboxes).
  - Fields to include: date_range, invoice_id, subscription_id, project_id, team_id, cost_center, model_name, tokens_charged, token_cost_usd, infra_cost_usd, accelerator_surcharge_usd, credits_applied_usd, net_cost_usd, forecast_30d_usd, forecast_60d_usd, forecast_90d_usd, remaining_budget_usd, budget_id, allocation_path
  - Export options: timezone, currency, group_by (daily/weekly/monthly), include_zero_rows toggle, include_raw_kv_cache_events toggle.
  - Right column: Alerting configuration panel. Top-level toggle (enabled/disabled).
    - Scope selector: single budget | multiple budgets | global
    - Condition builder: (metric) [rolling 7d avg spend | 24h spend | forecast_overrun_probability] (operator) [>=, >, <=] (value) [fixed USD or % of budget]
    - Heuristics: smoothing window (defaults: 3 days), min-data-days (default 3), cooldown period (default 24h), suppression if single-day spike > X% but returns below threshold next day
    - Notification targets: email, webhooks, Slack channel (select from org integrations). Multi-target with escalation delays.

ALERTING HEURISTICS (detailed proposals)
- Baseline algorithm: use rolling average of net_cost_usd over lookback_window to avoid single-day anomalies. Default lookback = min(7 days, budget window length).
- Forecast-trigger: compute probability that projected cumulative spend will exceed budget within the budget window using simple linear extrapolation + variance from past 14-day residuals. Fire when probability > 70% (configurable).
- Spike suppression: if day_t0 > threshold but rolling_avg(t0..t-2) < threshold * 0.6, suppress and create a low-priority notification (event logged) instead of alerting.
- Deduping & grouping: group events by allocation_path + model_name within 6h window; incremental summary notification rather than many separate alerts.

EXPORT CSV SHAPE (example header)
- Suggested header row exactly as: date_range,invoice_id,subscription_id,allocation_path,project_id,team_id,cost_center,model_name,tokens_charged,token_cost_usd,infra_cost_usd,accelerator_surcharge_usd,credits_applied_usd,net_cost_usd,forecast_30d_usd,forecast_60d_usd,forecast_90d_usd,remaining_budget_usd
- Notes: allocation_path is a pipe-delimited string representing the hierarchy (e.g., "org|dev-platform|ml-team|search-recs"). Avoid nested JSON in cell.

EDGE CASES
- Budgets with multiple currencies: exports should normalize to a selected output currency using daily FX rate (include fx_date and fx_rate columns if currency conversion used).
- Retroactive adjustments/credits applied after export time: exports are snapshots; include exported_at timestamp and a flag showing whether invoice is final.
- Missing allocation metadata: fallback to subscription-level attribution and mark rows with allocation_path = "unattributed".

METRICS / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Export success: users can generate a CSV with forecast columns correctly populated for 95% of accounts in staging.
- Alert precision: reduce acknowledged false-positive alerts by at least 40% compared to baseline fixed-threshold alerts in the canary cohort.
- UI flows: new Exports & Alerts tab implemented, accessible within three clicks from Budgets list.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED
- Forecast model: start with linear extrapolation + variance vs. building ARIMA/prophet in product? (engineering prefers simple first; research wants a later plugin).
- Export retention: how long do we keep precomputed forecast snapshots? default 90 days? (privacy/space tradeoff)
- Multi-currency conversion: use enterprise FX provider vs. internal simple daily rates?

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES / ENGINEERING CONSIDERATIONS
- Backend: add new export endpoint with streaming CSV generation. Endpoint must accept fields list and timezone/currency params. Consider using worker job for large exports (async export with download link).
- Forecast compute: on-demand vs. precompute. Recommendation: compute on-demand for ad-hoc exports; precompute nightly forecast for frequently used budgets to keep exports fast.
- Alerts: use the existing notifications framework; add grouping key = budget_id + allocation_path + model_name. Track last_alerted_at in DB to enforce cooldowns.

GROOMING / BACKLOG ITEMS (rough tickets)
- INF-2312 export: csv schema + backend streaming (owner: Miguel)
- INF-2417 alerts: heuristic engine + UI (owner: Evelyn)
- INF-2450 wireframes and copy (owner: design)

NEXT STEPS
- Design: produce 2 polished mock variants (compact vs detailed) for review by 2025-03-12.
- Eng: spike to implement streaming CSV prototype and linear-forecast for single budget by 2025-03-19.
- PM: align on default heuristic thresholds and notification templates; prepare canary cohort list (target 10 major customers).

NOTES TO SELF (work-in-progress)
- Slack thread: #billing-product (see thread pinned messages) contains user requests and sample CSVs from customers.
- Bring up multi-currency decision in architecture sync next Tues.

REFERENCES
- Jira: INF-2312, INF-2417, INF-2450
- GitHub: console PR 487 (early export UI)
summary: Working doc for new budget exports + smarter alert heuristics: wireframes, CSV schema, algorithm proposals, backlog tickets, and next steps
